column1: # Which version file owns which consumer. scripts/toolchain-drift-check.sh reads
# this table and nothing else to decide where an Erlang/Elixir version may live.
# Columns: <owner> <consumer>, whitespace-separated, one consumer a row. The
# owner is a *.tool-versions file, or `data`.
#   .github/workflows/X.yml       every erlef/setup-beam step in X reads the file
#                                 with `version-file:` + `version-type: strict`
#   .github/workflows/X.yml#job   the same, for one job; beats the workflow row
#   .github/actions/X/action.yml  the same, for a composite action
#   */Dockerfile, *.sh, ...       a version on a line naming a tool equals that
#                                 tool's number here, or the file reads this
#                                 file by path
#   *.tool-versions               that file's erlang and elixir lines equal this
#                                 file's, unless a pin row names the number
#   data <file> <reason>          a test or fixture file whose versions are test
#                                 data or past check names, not a runtime. A data
#                                 row covers EVERY number in its file, an install
#                                 line too, so the check allows one only on the
#                                 paths its own test-path rule names: *.test.sh,
#                                 *_test.*, test/, tests/, fixtures/. A test file
#                                 that sets up a tool for anything but its own
#                                 test takes line rows instead
#   pin <file> <token> <what>     one token that is not an owned tool's version
#   line <file> <hash> <words> :: <reason>
#                                 one line whose numbers are not versions
# Every tracked .tool-versions / *.tool-versions must appear here. A version on
# a line that names erlang, otp, elixir or node (or any tool an owner file
# names), and any image tag, in a workflow, action, container or compose file,
# deploy file, script, Makefile or mise config, fails without a row. A number
# on a line that names no tool is not seen (task-1c24786728762c92). Moving a
# consumer to another file is editing its row; folding a version file into
# another is deleting its rows and re-pointing its consumers.
# The content server's runtime: asdf on the box resolves the repo-root file.

# The release images: the control plane builds cloud/Dockerfile, and
